ideas.truth: The thing that finally gets you moving again after being stuck for years isn't hope alone — it's finding you were already equipped the whole time.
ideas.moment: A castaway digs a weathered Mokobara bag out of the sand and unzips it to find his wife's photo tucked among supplies he'd forgotten he packed.
ideas.key_frame: Sand-crusted hands unzipping a Mokobara bag on a golden-hour beach, a photo corner just visible inside.

ideas.truth: We laugh at the moment we realise the thing we underestimated was carrying more than we ever gave it credit for.
ideas.moment: The castaway keeps pulling item after item — food, rope, a machete, tools, and finally a photo — out of one bag, stacking an absurd pile beside him, laughing in disbelief.
ideas.key_frame: A castaway surrounded by a growing pile of gear, still reaching into one open Mokobara bag for more.

ideas.truth: Home is something we keep alive in our heads long before we physically get there.
ideas.moment: A single Mokobara bag sits at the tideline under moonlight, unzipped just enough for a photograph to glow faintly against the packed supplies inside — no person shown.
ideas.key_frame: A lit, unattended bag at the shoreline at night, a photo's edge glowing from the opening.

why: It's the only idea built around demonstration, not assertion — the joke IS the capacity, which makes the brand load-bearing to the story (Contagious test), and it directly satisfies the customer's funniest ask (weapons included) without needing wives-as-props or Greek costuming to land. It's crafted for the frequent traveler who's been caught under-packed before and wants proof the bag can carry more than they'd ever expect.
treatment: A weather-beaten castaway digs a sand-buried Mokobara bag out of the beach at golden hour and unzips it with a gasp — it's still here. He starts pulling gear out: canned food, coiled rope, a machete, a fishing spear, dried fruit — more and more, stacking an impossible pile beside him, laughing at how much keeps coming. Then he finds a small photograph tucked inside, looks at it quietly, tucks it into his shirt, and — bag already zipped and slung over his shoulder — walks toward a driftwood raft at the shoreline as the sun drops low, the bag riding on his back — the last thing we see before the logo.

scenes.prompt: Low, slow push-in handheld shot at golden hour. A weather-beaten castaway in his forties, salt-crusted beard, sun-bleached torn shirt, rolled cargo pants, hollow eyes turning hopeful, digs both hands into the sand and pulls free a weather-worn Mokobara bag, its brass emblem catching the low sun as sand cascades off, unzipping it partway — one continuous action, 8 seconds. Deserted tropical beach, old shipwreck debris and a crude driftwood shelter in the background hinting at years stranded. Warm golden-hour light, gritty survival-film texture; sound of wind, distant waves, sand sliding, a zipper pulling open.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: Close-up, sand-caked hands mid-dig, fingertips just closing around the top edge of the bag half-buried in wet sand, the embossed Mokobara emblem visible on the flap, golden-hour light raking across the beach.

scenes.prompt: Static medium shot with a slight rack focus. The same weather-beaten castaway reaches into the same open Mokobara bag again and again, pulling out canned food, a coiled rope, a small machete, a fishing spear, dried fruit and a folded net, stacking a growing, almost absurd pile beside him and laughing in disbelief at how much more keeps coming — one continuous action, 8 seconds. Same beach, pile growing in the foreground, the bag's tan leather and brass emblem centre-frame. Bright, comedic energy; sound of rustling gear, soft clinks, his own surprised laughter, waves behind him.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: Wide-medium shot, castaway crouched beside the open bag, a modest pile of supplies (rope, tin, machete handle visible) already stacked next to him, hand mid-reach back into the bag, brand emblem visible on the flap.

scenes.prompt: Slow-motion tracking shot from the side, moving with the subject. The same weather-beaten castaway, bag already zipped and slung over one shoulder, holds a small photograph in his free hand and looks at it with quiet longing as he walks steadily toward a driftwood raft at the shoreline, tucking the photo into his shirt just before he reaches the water's edge — one continuous walking action, 8 seconds. Same beach, crude raft of driftwood and cloth waiting at the water's edge, sun low on the horizon, the bag lit as the hero object against the sunset. Warm, hopeful tone; sound of waves, wind, a soft swelling score.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: Side profile, castaway mid-stride with the zipped, brand-emblem-visible bag on his shoulder, photograph held in his other hand, raft and sunset visible ahead of him.

finish.copy_placement: Lower-third supers added in post: brand name and one short line ('Packed for whatever's next.') appearing over scene 3 as he walks, so the film reads with sound off; logo introduced only as a static end card, never asked of the model. Line is written for the frequent traveler who's been caught under-packed before and wants proof the bag can carry more than expected.
finish.end_card: Clean end card: the Mokobara bag on a plain background (product shot matching reference photos exactly), logo and tagline beneath, no other elements.
finish.music: Sparse acoustic guitar under scenes 1–2 building into a warm, swelling orchestral cue by scene 3 to carry the hope-of-homecoming beat.
